observations: Photo 0 shows the back of a black Samsung smartphone held in a hand; the word SAMSUNG is printed near the bottom.
The rear camera module has four lenses arranged vertically on the upper left, with a flash and sensor beside them.
Two orange sticky notes with handwritten figures are attached to the back, partially covering the surface.
A watermark reads SEADOT GROUP POSTED ON JIJI across the lower half of both photos.
Photo 1 shows the same phone in front of a glass display cabinet filled with many other boxed and unboxed phones.
The front screen, ports, buttons, battery health, and any model number beyond Samsung are not visible in either photo.

Origin and usage history cannot be determined from photos.
SAMSUNG is readable on the back, but Galaxy S23 Ultra is not visible in the photos.
Logistics and pickup arrangements cannot be confirmed from photos.

risks.proof: Photo of the Settings > About phone screen showing the exact model number, or a photo of the box/IMEI label.
risks.if_unproven: priced as an unverified Samsung smartphone, not an S23 Ultra

risks.risk: The phone may not power on or may have hidden faults.

risks.risk: The sticky notes may be hiding cracks, repairs, or replaced parts.
risks.proof: Close-up photos with the sticky notes removed, or photos of the areas beneath them.

risks.risk: The device may be carrier-locked, blacklisted, or have a bad IMEI.

Video of the phone powering on and navigating the home screen
